heroHeadline: SAC Recaptures Maw Taung and Tonzang — Twin Territorial Reversals as Junta Pushes Multi-Front May Offensive; AA Advances on Chinese CMEC Port at Kyaukphyu — Day 1,935
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,935 of Myanmar's civil war (May 21, 2026), the junta completed twin recaptures on May 19: Maw Taung — KNLA Brigade 4's strategic Thailand border crossing in Tanintharyi Region, held by the Karen resistance since November 2025 — and Tonzang in northern Chin State, held by Chin joint forces since May 2024. The back-to-back territorial reversals are the most significant junta gains since the Falam recapture (April 25-26) and reflect a sustained SAC offensive surge across Myanmar's western and southern fronts in May 2026. Thousands of civilians remain displaced near the Ranong-Thailand border from the Maw Taung offensive. Meanwhile, the Arakan Army continues advancing on Kyaukphyu — the site of China's $7.3-billion CMEC deep-sea port project — with SAC jets and warships bombarding Sanae Township and destroying 100+ homes on May 21, displacing over 50,000 civilians. China, whose strategic investments are directly threatened by the AA's Kyaukphyu offensive, endorsed the SAC during Wang Yi's Naypyidaw visit in April 2026. Separately, TNLA rejected China-brokered junta demands at Kunming talks (May 12-13) to surrender four northern Shan State towns, while PDF forces captured the Saing Pyin police station in Depayin Township, Sagaing, on May 14-16 (11 junta killed). The conflict's simultaneous multi-front nature — SAC gains in Tanintharyi and Chin, resistance pressure in Sagaing and Kachin, escalating crisis in Rakhine — continues to produce a massive humanitarian emergency with 3.6 million displaced and no ceasefire in sight.
